main_body: Snow-covered conifer: a stacked cone of dark green foliage tiers with snow bands draped across each tier, and a small brown trunk at the base.
top_band: none; the column scan shows alternating snow bands (L 200-249) and dark green foliage (L 27-57) with no single top surface above a front face. These are snow drapes across a cone, not a horizontal top surface.
evidence: This is an organic tree. The cone silhouette uses alternating snow and foliage bands, and each snow band reads as a diagonal drape over the branches, so there is no flat horizontal top to judge. Ordinary conifer drawing is plausible for an organic object. There is no isometric side face and no box-like structure that would fail the contract. The foliage reads as a volume lit from the upper left, so I treat the contract as not applicable and pass it.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 13 distinct colours and a median of 8 colours per tile, against 108-109 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references. Snow has about 3 steps (white, light blue, blue-grey) and the foliage about 3-4 dark greens. The outline is a dark navy-green tint (0% neutral), so it is tinted rather than pure black. The foliage has a few dot highlights, but large areas are flat dark green, notably the right half of each tier, which forms a vertical split. The cone is a rigid geometric triangle with a regular scalloped edge, much simpler than the references' organic leaf clumps. It looks flatter and thinner than the reference, so it fails.
